title: Winding a Bedside Alarm Clock

focus: The setting is winding a Bedside Alarm Clock. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Clock signal that wakes a sleeper

answerNotes.CLOCK: A clock shows time. The hour hand moves more slowly than the minute hand on a traditional clock face.
answerNotes.HAND: Hand can name a body part or a clock pointer. A clock's minute hand makes a full turn each hour.
answerNotes.FACE: Face can name the front of a head or the marked surface of a clock. The surrounding objects identify the sense used in the clue.
answerNotes.DIAL: A dial can show numbers on a clock, telephone, or radio. Its marks identify times, phone choices, or station frequencies according to the object.
answerNotes.WIND: Wind has two pronunciations and meanings: moving air, or turning something around a center. A yarn ball or clock uses the turning action.
answerNotes.HOUR: An hour contains sixty minutes. A minute contains sixty seconds; these two relationships are easy to mix up.
answerNotes.BELL: A bell rings when a clapper or striker vibrates it. A school bell and a decorative handbell use that same basic sound-making idea.

answerNotes.DIAL: A dial can show numbers on a clock, telephone, or radio. Its marks identify times, phone choices, or station frequencies according to the object.

answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.HOT: Hot describes temperature. A hot dog is a food name, so the two-word phrase has a meaning beyond the adjective alone.
answerNotes.CLOCK: A clock shows time. The hour hand moves more slowly than the minute hand on a traditional clock face.
